name: Moon-forming impact
blurb: The proto-Earth struck by Theia, a body near the mass of Mars, at the speed it falls from far away and at 45 degrees: the canonical giant impact (Canup 2004). Both are iron-alloy cores under rock mantles with ANEOS equations of state. Rock from both is thrown into orbit; the Moon gathers from that disk. Lengths in Earth radii, masses in Earth masses; a time unit is 13.4 minutes, so a day is 107.

featured.label: Theia’s mass (M⊕)
featured.tip: The impactor’s mass, in Earth masses: 0.11 is Mars. Changing it starts the run again

featured.label: Impact parameter
featured.tip: Pericenter distance of the parabolic orbit over the sum of the two radii, which is the square of the sine of the angle at which they touch: 0 is head-on, 0.5 is 45 degrees, 1 just grazes. Changing it starts the run again
